data.name: Floriano
data.gender_notes: Floriano is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'florianus', meaning 'flowering, blooming'. In Christian tradition, Floriano is a name of a saint, believed to have lived in the 3rd century, who was martyred during the persecutions of Emperor Diocletian. The name Floriano carries the meaning “Flowery, blooming” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Floriano usually hope their child will grow to embody flowery, blooming and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Floriano belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Flowery, blooming.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Floriano total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: פלווריאנו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פלווריאנו נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'פלוריאנוס', שמשמעותה 'פורח' או 'פרח'. שם זה קשור למושג הפריחה והצמיחה, ויכול לסמל את התחדשות האביב והחיים. בהקשר הנוצרי, השם עשוי להתייחס לתחייתו של ישו ולקדושים ששמותיהם קשורים לפריחה וצמיחה רוחנית.

in_greek.name: Φλωριανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Φλωριανός προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'Florlanus', που σημαίνει 'άνθος' ή 'αυτό που ανθίζει'. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την ιδέα της ανθοφορίας και της πνευματικής ανάπτυξης. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοιες λέξεις σχετίζονται με την πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την αναγέννηση μέσω της πίστης.

in_latin.name: Floriano
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Floriano derivatur a latino 'florens' vel 'florianus', quod significat 'florem' aut 'qui floret'. Hoc nomen ad vitam et incrementum refertur, et in traditione christiana potest significare resurrectionem et vitam aeternam.

historical_references.reference: Floriano de la Vega, a Spanish military leader and governor, led the defense of Zaragoza against the French army in 1413 during the War of the Bands. He was later made the Duke of Valencia and played an important role in King Ferdinand I's reign.

Florianus, a Roman Christian martyr, was a bishop of the city of Amiens in Gaul during the late 3rd century. He was executed during the persecutions of Emperor Diocletian for his refusal to renounce Christianity.

In folklore, Florian de la Vega is a character from Brazilian mythology who represents prosperity, abundance and good fortune.
